[antonlabz] I was also in the first batch to get one of these and have no regretted it at all. The Pro model is enough for 99% of games you'll realistically play on it; I think the Max is a bit overkill, maybe just for enthusiasts who really want to squeeze out every drop of performance and plan to emulate some heavy PC games.
Even if you've been in the emulation/retro handheld scene for some time, this has been one of the best purchase I've ever made in this space.
The dual-screen form factor makes it perfect for playing NDS/3DS games the way it should be, and even then it's powerful enough to emulate virtually any other console that's currently possible with a beautiful OLED screen, including PC games.
There have been a few of these dual-screen handhelds released, but the Thor is by far the most successful, with good reason. Everything from the small design choices, specs, dimensions, are basically perfect.
Probably the only complaint I have (and seen) are the L2/R2 buttons feeling a little bit awkward to press, and the back being flat. But the buttons complaint is very minor and the ergonomics is so easily fixed with a grip (I'd recommend a 3rd party one, the official one kinda sucks).

[Iwantthebestprice] Can someone fill me in, is this basically like a 3DS or something and all games come pre loaded or can be downloaded? Why are people buying this?
[despavr] Its an android in the shape of a 3DS, but so powerful it can even emulate nintendo switch games perfectly fine.
There aren't many handheld gaming devices that can do such emulation and ESPECIALLY in a clamshell design like the nintendo DS.
People are buying it because it can even run their steam games. I have a similar device (lower spec'd) and i run steam games on it even though it is an android through an app called gamehub.
For example, I played 3-4 hours of Persona 5 on steam on a similar handheld from this brand on a flight recently. The saves and achievements are all synced with my steam account and desktop version of the game.
Basically, if you want a handheld gaming device but aren't into the steam deck style and size, this is an awesome option.
[Chad0s] how long does cashback to appear usually take?
[Smigit] Where’s Azahar and the drivers at in relation to shader compilation stutter and the like?
I have an Odin 2 Portal and it runs most systems really well, but as recently as I guess 6 months ago, 3DS is a system I haven’t enjoyed emulating on an Android device as some of the games I was playing had quite severe compilation stutters and it killed the experience. While you can play through it and cache those shaders, I want that first playthrough to be one where I’m not being taken out of the game due to constant stuttering.
So far I’ve found playing on an actual 3DS to be better than playing via emulation for that console specifically, but been a few months since I last tried it all out. Screens not as nice, but things were smoother when played on a New 3DS model.
Curious if things have progressed a lot in 2026 in this space or not.
